questions.question: When is a set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ convex?
options: When every whole line through two points of $C$ lies in $C$
When the midpoint of some pair of points of $C$ is in $C$
When $\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\in C$ for all $x,y\in C$, $\lambda\in[0,1]$
When $C$ contains $0$ and is closed under addition

questions.question: If $C_1$ and $C_2$ are convex subsets of $\mathbb R^n$, which set is always convex?
options: $C_1\cap C_2$
$C_1\cup C_2$
$\mathbb R^n\setminus C_1$
$C_1\setminus C_2$

questions.question: Why is the unit circle $\{(x,y):x^2+y^2=1\}$ not convex?
options: Because it is bounded but does not contain the origin
Because it is a closed subset of the plane
Because it has an empty interior in the plane
Because a chord from $(1,0)$ to $(-1,0)$ leaves it

questions.question: Which subset of $\mathbb R^2$ is not convex?
Is the open half-plane $\{(x,y):x+y<1\}$ convex?
options: No: a strict inequality destroys convexity
No: an unbounded set cannot be convex
Yes: averaging keeps the sum below $1$
No: it is not closed under addition, as $(0.6,0)+(0.6,0)$ shows

questions.question: For $x=(1,3)$, $y=(5,-1)$ and $\lambda=\tfrac14$, what is the point $\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y$?
Which of these subsets of $\mathbb R^2$ is convex?
Let $C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x\le0,\ x\ge1\}$. Is $C$ empty, and is it convex?
options: $C$ is empty and convex
$C$ is empty and not convex
$C$ is non-empty and convex
$C$ is non-empty and not convex

questions.question: Is the region $\{(x,y):x+2y\le8,\ 3x+y\le9,\ x\ge0,\ y\ge0\}$ convex?
options: No, since the region has several corners
Only if the region happens to be bounded
Yes, as an intersection of half-planes
No, since several constraints define it

questions.question: Does the set $C=\{(x,y):x\ge0,\ y\ge0,\ x+y=1\}$ satisfy the definition of convexity?
options: No: it is only a segment, with no interior
No: an equality constraint destroys convexity
Only once its two endpoints are removed
Yes: a line intersected with two half-planes

questions.question: For a non-empty set $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, replace the convexity condition by $\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y\in C$ for every $x,y\in C$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Which sets satisfy this stronger condition?
options: Exactly the affine subspaces
Exactly the convex sets
Exactly the vector subspaces containing $0$
Exactly the bounded convex sets

questions.question: If $C$ is convex and $x,y,z\in C$, does $\tfrac13x+\tfrac13y+\tfrac13z$ lie in $C$?
options: Not necessarily: convexity only controls pairs of points
Yes: apply the two-point condition twice
Only if the three points lie on one line
Only if the set also contains its boundary

questions.question: For a convex function $f\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ and a number $c$, is the sublevel set $\{x:f(x)\le c\}$ convex?
options: Only if $f$ is a linear function
No: sublevel sets of convex functions can have holes
Only for values $c\ge0$
Yes, by the convexity inequality for $f$

questions.question: Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ be convex and set $D=\{x+(3,-2):x\in C\}$. What is guaranteed?
options: $D$ is convex
$D$ contains the origin
$D$ is closed
$C\cup D$ is convex

questions.question: For which $\lambda\in[0,1]$ does $\lambda(2,0)+(1-\lambda)(0,2)$ lie on the circle $x^2+y^2=4$?
options: For every single $\lambda\in[0,1]$
Only for the midpoint, $\lambda=\tfrac12$
Only for $\lambda=0$ and $\lambda=1$
For no $\lambda$ in $[0,1]$ at all

questions.question: For which $a$ is $(-\infty,0]\cup[a,\infty)\subseteq\mathbb R$ convex?
options: For every value of $a$
Exactly for $a\le0$
Exactly for $a\ge0$
For no value of $a$

questions.question: If $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is convex and $M$ is an $m\times n$ matrix, is the image $\{Mx:x\in C\}$ convex?
options: Only if the matrix $M$ is invertible
No: linear maps can bend segments
Only if $M$ is square, $m=n$
Yes, since $M$ maps segments to segments

questions.question: The convex function $f(x)=(x-2)^2$ is minimised over $C=[0,1]\cup[2.5,5]$. What can be said about $x=1$?
options: Local but not global: $f(2.5)<f(1)$
Global, because $f$ is convex
Not even local, as $f'(1)\ne0$
Global, because $C$ is closed and $f$ is continuous

questions.question: Within the positive quadrant, is $S=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ xy\ge1\}$ a convex set?
options: No: $(1,1)$ and $(-1,-1)$ have the midpoint $(0,0)$
Yes: it lies above the convex graph of $1/x$
No: its boundary curve $xy=1$ is not straight
No: $xy$ is not a convex function

questions.question: For convex $C_1,C_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, is the sum $C_1+C_2=\{a+b:a\in C_1,\ b\in C_2\}$ convex?
options: Only if the two convex sets are equal
No: sums of convex sets can have holes
Yes: combinations of sums split into sums
Only if both sets contain the origin $0$
